newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks firmer, but fading in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks firmer, but fading in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices were slightly higher but fading from early highs in late Wednesday trade as profit-taking took a bite of a five-day rally, brokers said.
With 55 minutes left, at 0305 GMT, the index was up 13.46 points or 0.16 percent at 8,692.70, off a high of 8,753.89.
As on Tuesday, turnover again was heavy at T$141 billion.
Electronics, which had led recent gains, were up 3.37 percent, with computer giant Acer up T$4 to T$89.5.
Opto-electronics and power supply maker Liton was up the daily seven percent limit to T$106 on its ex-bonus issue date.
The electronics surge failed to carry other sectors, with financials, textiles, constructions and steels all falling.

"Buying is now focused too much on electronics, especially semiconductor shares, as investors are buying the sector for a 1998 dream, expecting its sound outlook then," said National Securities manager Allen Huang.
"But sometimes I wonder whether electronics' recent surges haven't been too much?" he said.
Several brokers said they nevertheless expected a firming trend to test 9,000 soon.
